summary: Automates browser workflows with LLMs and computer vision, so tasks keep working on new sites and after layout changes.

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Skyvern automates tasks in a web browser using large language models and computer vision instead of fixed CSS or XPath selectors. A group of agents looks at the page, plans and carries out actions, so one workflow can work on websites it has never seen and keep working when layouts change. It offers a Playwright-compatible Python SDK that adds AI commands such as act, extract, validate and natural-language clicks, plus a local server and web UI. A managed Skyvern Cloud version is also available.
sixtySeconds.problem: Traditional browser scripts break whenever a site's layout changes and need custom code per site. Skyvern reasons about the page visually instead.
whoFor: Developers automating form filling and web tasks
Ops teams running repetitive browser workflows
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it when you need browser automation that adapts to unfamiliar or changing sites, self-hosted or in the cloud.
requirements: On Windows: Rust and VS Code C++ build tools with the Windows SDK
Or Docker Desktop for the full containerized setup

overview: Install with pip install "skyvern[server]" and run skyvern quickstart; it uses a local SQLite database by default.
The pip package has no web UI; for the UI, use Docker Compose, which runs Postgres, the API and the UI together at localhost:8080.
Use the Python SDK to mix normal Playwright calls with AI actions. AGPL-3.0 licensed; Skyvern Cloud is the hosted option.

tutorial.title: Add AI actions to a Playwright script

steps.title: Start locally
steps.body: from skyvern import Skyvern; skyvern = Skyvern.local().

steps.title: Get a page
steps.body: browser = await skyvern.launch_cloud_browser(); page = await browser.get_working_page(); await page.goto("https://example.com").

steps.title: Use AI actions
steps.body: Mix normal calls like page.click("#login-button") with page.click(prompt="Add first item to cart") or page.agent.run_task(...).
